subject: Discovery recap: BrightCart — embeddings & rerank (index scale, latency/cost targets)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@brightcart.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery recap: BrightCart — embeddings & rerank (index scale, latency/cost targets)

Alex — thanks for the time today. As promised, high-level recap from our call and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned.

Summary of pain & goals
- Pain: Search relevance has degraded at scale; current ranked results rely on BM25 + light ML reranking and misses long-tail queries.
- Goal: Improve relevance and freshness for product search and recommendations while keeping latency/cost within strict targets (see below).

Current stack (what you told us)
- Source: BrightCart product catalog + clickstream + user signals (approx. 5–10M SKUs historically, active index ~50M vectors including embeddings + variants).
- Vector store: Pinecone (mostly managed small pods today).
- Serving: Combination of synchronous queries for search and async batch jobs for recommendations.

Success criteria (what would be considered a win)
- Precision/recall: measurable lift in recall@10 and NDCG vs baseline on your eval set.
- Latency: 95th percentile online rerank end-to-end (query -> scored results) < 120ms for 90% of traffic (ideal target <100ms).
- Cost: per-query incremental cost increase < 2x current infra cost (targeting cost parity with batching/prefix cache optimizations).

Workload patterns and scale notes
- Index scale: ~50M vectors (mix of 1536- to 3072-dim embeddings).
- Query pattern: Heavy tail — 70% low-fanout queries (single shard), 30% high-fanout personalization queries. Peak QPS during promotions ~3–4x baseline.
- Batch behavior: Nightly re-embed for new/updated SKUs (full sync weekly), streaming small updates throughout the day.

Initial recommendations (from Redwood)
- Evaluate approximate nearest neighbor config tuned for latency: quantized HNSW variants + sharded routing for hot partitions.
- Use per-route prefix/KV caching for popular queries and caching of candidate sets before rerank to reduce compute.
- Consider a hybrid flow: cheap candidate retrieval (ANN) + small transformer reranker on GPU for top-K to control cost/latency tradeoff.

Next steps (agreed)
1) Alex: share system inventory + sample eval queries/ground truth (you mentioned you can get a small test set).
2) BrightCart: share current Pinecone pod sizing and typical QPS by endpoint (attachment would be fine).
3) Redwood: run feasibility eval on a small subset (we’ll ingest a test index and run a 24–48h traffic replay to report latency/cost estimates).
4) Schedule technical deep dive with Dev (SE) next week to go over shard/layout and routing policies.

Attachments I requested: system inventory spreadsheet, sample eval queries (see list below). I’ll compile Redwood’s initial eval plan and send a calendar invite for the deep dive.

Thanks again — excited to help BrightCart tighten rerank quality without blowing up costs.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0147

Thanks Marissa — great summary and exactly what we needed to capture. Quick answers and a couple notes:

- Inventory: attaching an export of our system inventory and current Pinecone config. The index size numbers are in the sheet (active ~48M vectors, historical deltas kept in cold storage).
- Eval set: Priya will pull a 10k query sample + relevance judgments and share by EOD tomorrow.
- Timeline: procurement is targeting an initial POC in Q2; we’d like a 6–8 week POC window if the numbers look reasonable.

Question for Redwood: do you have any preliminary guesses on whether a hybrid ANN + small transformer reranker will meet our 95p < 120ms target at 50M index size on managed Dedicated capacity? We understand rough estimates are fine now; we mainly want to know if the approach is viable before we invest in the POC.

Attached: brightcart_system_inventory.xlsx

Alex Johnson

alex.johnson@brightcart.com | (212) 555-0199

Alex — quick technical follow-up from our SE side after reviewing the inventory you sent. I’m keeping this high-level for now; we’ll deep-dive on the technical call.

Notes:
- 50M vectors at 1536–3072 dims: with quantized HNSW and sharded routing we expect candidate retrieval 95p in the 20–60ms range depending on shard layout and node CPU/GPU mix.
- Reranker: small transformer rerank (distilled T5 variant) for top-50 candidates can be served on GPU with batching; expect 95p additional latency ~30–80ms depending on batch size and GPU type.
- Combined: With smart routing (send high-fanout queries to a more parallelized path) and prefix caching for hot queries, meeting 95p <120ms is plausible on Dedicated with appropriate pod sizing.

What I need from you for a realistic POC estimate:
- Sample query QPS by endpoint & % of high-fanout queries
- Ground truth eval (even small) so we can compute lift vs baseline and tune K for tradeoffs
- Any SLAs/penalties that would be required for production.

I’ll drop more concrete node/pod sizing in the technical call materials. If you’re open, I’ll propose a config with two routing tiers (latency-critical + cost-optimized) and a sample cost estimate for a 50M index.

—
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.com
